name: Genetic Porokeratosis

criteria.description: Presence of cornoid lamella on histopathological examination
Characteristic annular plaques with raised keratotic borders
Positive family history of porokeratosis or similar lesions
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with porokeratosis (e.g., MVK, SLC17A9, or others)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation of cornoid lamella
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Annular plaques with raised keratotic borders
searchTerms: circular skin lesions with raised edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cornoid lamella observed on skin biopsy
searchTerms: distinctive scale layer on skin sample

pathognomonic.symptomName: Peripheral expansion of lesions with central atrophy
searchTerms: skin lesions growing outward with center thinning
expanding patches with central skin loss
peripheral lesion growth and central atrophy
skin lesions mainly on sun-exposed areas
rash appearing on face and arms

occasional.symptomName: Development of squamous cell carcinoma within lesions
searchTerms: squamous cell carcinoma in skin patches
nail abnormalities linked to skin lesions
swollen lymph nodes due to cancer

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as fever related to secondary infection
searchTerms: fever and systemic illness from infection
fever due to secondary skin infection

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in MVK, SLC17A9, or other associated genes
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with variable penetrance
Mutations in genes involved in keratinization pathways
other: Risk of malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma

distinguishingFeatures: Actinic keratosis lacks cornoid lamella histologically
Lesions are typically scaly erythematous patches rather than annular plaques with raised borders
Lichen planus presents with violaceous flat-topped papules
Absence of cornoid lamella and different histopathological features
Fungal infection confirmed by KOH preparation
Lesions usually respond to antifungal therapy

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or ulceration of lesions indicating possible malignant transformation
Persistent pain or bleeding from lesions
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Nofal A, et al. Porokeratosis: A Review of Clinical Features and Treatment. Dermatol Ther. 2018;31(6):e12691.
